lines.text: Blackout Brings
Creativity to Finals Week
A sudden power outage during finals week left Smithfield
students scrambling for solutions. Students took advantage
of their smart-phone flashlights, and university staff provided
camping lights for dorm lounges.
"It was stressful but kind of fun," said sophomore Grace Lee.
The blackout lasted six hours, caused by a transformer failure
near campus. Dining services offered free coffee, and
professors extended deadlines to ease the pressure.
"We made the best of it," said senior Omar Davis, who
studied with his bike light. Social media buzzed with photos
of candlelit study sessions, turning the inconvenience into a
moment of campus unity.
Some students even organized impromptu acoustic concerts
on the quad, proving that creativity thrives under constraints.
"It reminded us that community matters more than
convenience," said Professor Laura Chen.
By the early morning hours, power was restored, but the
evening's events left a lasting impression.
